title: Cloud Marketplace co-marketing sync (listing + customer story)
summary: Redwood and Nimbus aligned on a joint co-marketing package tied to Redwood’s upcoming Nimbus Cloud Marketplace listing. Nimbus requested a clear customer proof point (case study or lighter-weight customer story) to anchor the announcement and drive marketplace conversions. Redwood proposed using one of the design partners (Arcadia Health for Private/VPC or QuantaPay for Dedicated) depending on public-approval feasibility. The group agreed to target a late-July publish window, with an earlier “listing live” milestone possible if customer approvals slip. Nimbus reviewed required assets (marketplace listing copy, solution brief, customer quote approval, logos, security positioning, and a short demo video). Redwood flagged internal legal/compliance constraints and the need to avoid sensitive architecture/security details in public materials.
topics:
1) Timing: Nimbus marketplace review + co-marketing calendar
2) Announcement angle: marketplace listing + customer story (Private vs Dedicated)
3) Asset checklist: listing copy, images, solution brief, blog, press release/PR wire (optional)
4) Approvals: customer quote/logo release, Redwood legal and security review
5) Metrics claims: latency/cost phrasing and substantiation notes
6) Lead routing: marketplace leads, UTMs, and handoff to Redwood growth + sales
7) Contingency plan: if customer approval delays, publish a Redwood-only technical post + later customer addendum
next_steps: Redwood to send Nimbus a one-page launch brief (positioning, target dates, proposed customer story options) by 2025-06-20
Nimbus to send marketplace listing intake template + creative specs (image sizes, character limits, required fields) by 2025-06-19
Redwood to confirm which customer can be public by 2025-06-24 (Arcadia Health vs QuantaPay vs alternative)
Nimbus to tentatively reserve a co-marketing slot for week of 2025-07-28 pending approvals
Redwood to provide draft marketplace listing copy and solution brief outline by 2025-06-27
action_items: Ben Carter: Draft and share “Nimbus launch brief” (goals, narrative, timeline, asset list) — due 2025-06-20
Soojin Lee: Provide approved messaging blocks (production economics, reliability/fallbacks, deployment modes) + claim guardrails — due 2025-06-21
Tyler Benson: Create UTM plan + lead routing doc (who gets marketplace leads, Slack/email alerts, HubSpot source fields) — due 2025-06-25
Alex Chen: Send Nimbus marketplace listing requirements (fields, SLAs, security sections, review SLA) — due 2025-06-19
Priya Nair: Confirm Nimbus co-marketing formats available (blog, webinar, newsletter, social) + minimum customer proof requirement — due 2025-06-20
Ben Carter: Share 2 candidate customer story paths (Arcadia Health Private/VPC, QuantaPay Dedicated) with risk notes on approvals — due 2025-06-24
questions:
Nimbus: Do you require a named customer quote for the initial listing announcement, or is an anonymized performance story acceptable?
Redwood: What is the current marketplace review SLA from submission to live listing?
Nimbus: Can we run a two-step launch (listing live first, customer story later) and still qualify for the co-marketing slot?
Redwood: Are there restrictions on referencing regulated workloads (health/fintech) in public marketplace copy?
Nimbus: What are the requirements for security/compliance statements (SOC 2 wording, data retention language, VPC/private connectivity claims)?
transcript:
Nimbus Cloud Marketplace Co-Marketing Sync
Recorded by Fireflies.ai

Date: 2025-06-18
Start time: 9:00 AM PT
Duration: 42 min

Attendees:
- Ben Carter (Redwood Inference, Growth)
- Camila Reyes (Redwood Inference, VP Marketing)
- Soojin Lee (Redwood Inference, Product Marketing)
- Tyler Benson (Redwood Inference, Marketing Ops)
- Alex Chen (Nimbus Cloud Marketplace, Partner Marketing Lead)
- Priya Nair (Nimbus Cloud Marketplace, Partnerships)
- Jordan Ellis (Nimbus Cloud Marketplace, Solutions Architect)


[00:00] Ben Carter: Cool, alright. Thanks everyone for jumping on. This is the Nimbus marketplace co-marketing sync. Goal today: align on the announcement angle for the listing, and whether we can pair it with a customer story, and then just get super crisp on timelines and assets.

[00:17] Alex Chen: Sounds good. Thanks Ben. Yeah, from our side, we’re excited. We just need to make sure we have enough proof points for the “launch” package. Marketplace-only announcements can be a bit flat unless there’s a customer anchor.

[00:31] Camila Reyes: Totally. We’re running a structured reference program right now specifically to get those customer outcomes and approvals. So we can align those timelines.

[00:41] Priya Nair: Great. Maybe I’ll start with the Nimbus process so it’s clear. There’s basically two tracks: (1) marketplace listing review and (2) co-marketing editorial slot. The listing is a form + security + product copy. The co-marketing slot wants either a customer story, webinar, or joint blog.

[01:03] Ben Carter: Yup. And we’re trying to time it with our “case studies” section going live in docs and on the site.

[01:10] Jordan Ellis: Quick question before we go deep—are you listing as a managed API offering, or is this like a deployable into customer VPC type solution?

[01:19] Ben Carter: The first listing is for Redwood Hosted API and Redwood Dedicated as purchasable capacity through Nimbus. We can talk about Private, but we’re not making that a click-to-deploy SKU on day one. It’s more “contact sales.”

[01:37] Jordan Ellis: Okay, that helps. Then the copy should be careful: “Private deployment available” but not like “deploy in 10 minutes.”

[01:44] Soojin Lee: Exactly. We have guardrails there.

[01:48] Alex Chen: On the customer story piece—do you already have a named customer that’s willing to be public? Logo, quote, the whole thing.

[01:57] Camila Reyes: We have a couple in-flight. Two leading candidates: Arcadia Health, which is a regulated healthcare workload, and QuantaPay, fintech. Both are in approval workflows. Arcadia is more “Private / VPC / compliance.” QuantaPay is “Dedicated capacity / strict latency SLOs.”

[02:20] Alex Chen: If you had to pick today, which is more likely to clear approvals by end of July?

[02:26] Camila Reyes: Honestly, fintech sometimes moves faster on marketing than healthcare, but the healthcare story is very compelling for Nimbus buyers. We’re still validating.

[02:36] Ben Carter: We can also do a two-step. Listing goes live first, then the named case study follows when approvals clear.

[02:45] Priya Nair: That’s possible. For the co-marketing slot though, we typically want the customer story at the same time, or at least a “customer proof” element. It can be anonymized in some cases, but it depends.

[02:59] Alex Chen: Yeah, like, we can do “Customer spotlight” without naming them, but our editorial team will ask why it’s anonymous. If it’s “regulated environment,” that’s sometimes acceptable.

[03:12] Soojin Lee: If we go anonymized, we can still include specific metrics as ranges, as long as we can substantiate internally. But we need to avoid over-precise claims that imply we’re disclosing something sensitive.

[03:26] Jordan Ellis: Metrics is a big one. In marketplace listings, people want numbers. But we’ve seen launches get delayed because legal got nervous about “X% faster” claims.

[03:35] Camila Reyes: Yep. We’re building a metrics validation worksheet with SE ownership on methodology. So we can say, for example, “reduced p95 latency by ~30% in a replay benchmark” with footnote on window and workload.

[03:53] Ben Carter: To make this tangible: our preferred angle for Nimbus is “production economics” and “deployment flexibility” rather than “we have model X.” Buyers can get models anywhere.

[04:05] Alex Chen: That aligns with what performs well for us too. The category is crowded—AWS Bedrock, Replicate, Together, etc.—so the story has to be “why Redwood.”

[04:17] Soojin Lee: Exactly. For QuantaPay, the differentiator is predictable latency and burst handling on Dedicated, plus rollback/fallback policies. For Arcadia, it’s audit logs, key ownership, and VPC/private control plane patterns.

[04:33] Priya Nair: Let’s talk timeline. If we target late July, what are the key gating items on your side?

[04:39] Camila Reyes: Customer quote + logo release. That is the gating item. Also internal security review for what we say publicly about architecture and retention.

[04:49] Ben Carter: And then your marketplace review SLA. If we submit listing copy end of June, when could it be live?

[04:56] Priya Nair: Typical is 10 business days if everything is complete. If security questionnaire bounces back, it can stretch to three weeks.

[05:06] Tyler Benson: When you say “complete,” do you mean things like SOC report upload? Or just attestations.

[05:11] Priya Nair: It depends on the category. Usually: data handling, encryption, any compliance claims, and support SLAs. We don’t require you to upload SOC 2 publicly, but you need to describe.

[05:26] Jordan Ellis: Also, image requirements: you’ll need at least one product screenshot and a logo lockup. Character limits are strict.

[05:34] Ben Carter: Got it. We can deliver that.

[05:37] Alex Chen: For the co-marketing package, our standard “launch kit” includes: a joint blog post on Nimbus, optionally a press release (not always), a short solution brief PDF, and social copy. If you have a customer, we can do a 30-minute webinar too.

[05:57] Camila Reyes: Webinar might be too heavy for the first one. Our customers are bandwidth constrained. But blog + brief + customer quote feels doable.

[06:07] Soojin Lee: And we can do an architecture diagram, but it must be abstracted. No internal subnet details, no region specifics if they’re sensitive.

[06:17] Jordan Ellis: Yeah please don’t put CIDRs. (laughs)

[06:20] Ben Carter: Noted.

[06:22] Alex Chen: Can we align on what the “customer story” looks like? Like is it a full case study PDF, or a shorter spotlight?

[06:29] Camila Reyes: We can do both. Our internal program aims for a web story + PDF. But for Nimbus, we could do a shorter “spotlight” version—600 to 900 words—then link to the full case study if approved.

[06:44] Priya Nair: That’s good. Our editorial team likes shorter and punchier.

[06:49] Tyler Benson: For tracking: we’ll want UTMs on the Nimbus links, and we’ll want marketplace leads to route into HubSpot with a clear source.

[06:59] Alex Chen: We can pass leads via our standard partner lead share. It comes weekly, CSV, unless you’ve got the API integration.

[07:06] Tyler Benson: Weekly is fine for the first cut. We just need to align fields and ensure consent language.

[07:13] Ben Carter: Cool. Maybe we jump into the announcement narrative. So, “Redwood Inference now available on Nimbus Cloud Marketplace,” plus “Arcadia Health runs regulated LLM inference with Redwood Private” or “QuantaPay hits p95 under X with Dedicated.”

[07:31] Soojin Lee: Small correction: we probably shouldn’t say “under X” unless it’s fully validated and signed off. We can say “met sub-second p95 targets” or “improved p95 by 30%” depending on what they approve.

[07:44] Ben Carter: Yeah, fair.

[07:46] Alex Chen: What do you expect Nimbus customers to do after reading? Is it “buy Dedicated,” “try the API,” “talk to sales?”

[07:54] Ben Carter: Primary CTA: start with Hosted API, then path to Dedicated if they need predictable throughput. For enterprise, “contact sales for Dedicated/Private.”

[08:04] Jordan Ellis: Then in the listing, make sure there’s a clear “pricing model” section. Marketplace buyers bounce if it’s vague.

[08:12] Camila Reyes: We can provide a clear overview: usage-based for Hosted, reserved commits for Dedicated, and Private is enterprise licensing.

[08:22] Priya Nair: Great. On assets, here’s what we’ll need from Redwood for the co-marketing slot. I’ll send the official list, but roughly:
- Marketplace listing copy (short + long)
- Logo, 1-2 product screenshots
- Solution brief (2 pages)
- Joint blog post draft
- Customer quote + approvals
- Optional: 60-90 sec demo video

[08:49] Ben Carter: Video might be hard by July, but not impossible. We can do a lightweight screen capture of the Console: latency/cost breakdown, rollouts, fallback policy.

[09:00] Soojin Lee: If we do that, we must ensure no customer names appear in the Console view.

[09:05] Ben Carter: Yep.

[09:06] Alex Chen: That would help a lot. We can host it on the listing.

[09:11] Camila Reyes: Let’s talk approvals. If we pick Arcadia, they’ve already flagged they can’t share exact infrastructure details. They may allow “VPC deployment,” “customer-managed keys,” “audit logs exported,” but not which cloud, not which region.

[09:28] Jordan Ellis: That’s workable.

[09:30] Priya Nair: If the story is about regulated workloads, anonymity is more acceptable. But we still would like at least one named quote from a Redwood exec and a Nimbus quote.

[09:41] Camila Reyes: That’s fine. Jordan Blake can do an exec quote if needed.

[09:45] Alex Chen: Great. We also need someone from Redwood to be “spokesperson” for approvals—like one person who signs off on the final blog copy so we don’t get last-minute changes.

[09:56] Ben Carter: That can be Camila for marketing sign-off, and Soojin for messaging/claims. Legal review would be separate.

[10:05] Soojin Lee: Yep.

[10:07] Alex Chen: Cool.

[10:09] (crosstalk)

[10:10] Ben Carter: Sorry, Priya, go ahead.

[10:12] Priya Nair: I was just going to say, if the customer is named, we need the customer logo in addition to Redwood’s. If it’s anonymous, we can do “Customer in healthcare sector” but then we need stronger product visuals.

[10:27] Ben Carter: Makes sense.

[10:29] Tyler Benson: On the lead share: can you include a field that indicates whether they came from the blog vs the listing page? Or is it just marketplace interest.

[10:37] Alex Chen: Typically we tag by campaign. If we do a co-marketing campaign, it can be a separate source.

[10:44] Tyler Benson: Perfect.

[10:46] Ben Carter: Can we align on a target date? If we assume listing submission June 27, review completes around July 11-ish. Then we’d want content to publish… maybe week of July 28.

[11:01] Alex Chen: Week of July 28 works. That’s one of our open slots. Earlier is tough because we’re booked.

[11:07] Camila Reyes: Okay, pencil that.

[11:10] Soojin Lee: One thing: if QuantaPay is the customer story, there is an open support ticket about a latency regression during a benchmark window. It’s being resolved, but we shouldn’t lock claims until that’s closed and revalidated.

[11:25] Ben Carter: Yeah, good call.

[11:27] Alex Chen: That’s exactly the kind of thing that can become messy in public copy.

[11:31] Camila Reyes: Which is why Arcadia might actually be safer. Their story is less about one number and more about enabling Private deployment with compliance constraints.

[11:43] Jordan Ellis: Buyers on Nimbus do love the “compliance” story. If you can say “VPC/private networking,” “audit logs,” “KMS integration,” it’s compelling.

[11:54] Soojin Lee: We can say “integrates with customer-managed KMS/HSM.” We just need to confirm the exact phrasing.

[12:01] Priya Nair: Great. Also, please avoid saying “HIPAA compliant” unless you have a specific compliance posture statement.

[12:07] Camila Reyes: Yep, we won’t say HIPAA. We’ll say “supports regulated workloads” and list controls.

[12:14] Ben Carter: Okay. Can we talk about the solution brief structure? We can do: problem, why Redwood, deployment options, observability, security controls, and then a mini customer section.

[12:28] Alex Chen: Perfect. Keep it two pages. Our buyers don’t read 10-page PDFs.

[12:34] Ben Carter: Noted.

[12:36] Tyler Benson: For the marketplace listing, do you have a template we can fill? Character limits, etc.

[12:41] Priya Nair: Yes. I’ll send the intake template right after this call.

[12:46] Ben Carter: Thanks.

[12:48] Alex Chen: And for the blog, we can either have Redwood draft and we edit, or we draft and you edit. Usually partner drafts is faster.

[12:57] Camila Reyes: We can draft. We already have a narrative framework.

[13:02] Soojin Lee: We’ll draft with claim guardrails: “improved latency” must include measurement context, “reduced cost” must specify what cost metric (cost per 1k tokens or cost per query) and a window.

[13:16] Alex Chen: Great. That actually makes our legal team happier too.

[13:20] Ben Carter: Alright, let’s cover contingencies. If the customer approvals slip, we can still do a launch with Redwood-only content: “listing now live,” plus a technical blog about production inference economics, and then we update with the customer story later.

[13:36] Priya Nair: That can still qualify for co-marketing, but it might be a lighter slot—newsletter mention vs full blog.

[13:44] Camila Reyes: Understood.

[13:46] Jordan Ellis: One more thing: marketplace buyers ask about support and SLAs. Do you have standard SLAs for Dedicated?

[13:53] Ben Carter: For Dedicated we have SLA-backed uptime and latency targets; exact numbers depend on contract. We can phrase it as “SLA options available.”

[14:04] Soojin Lee: We should avoid quoting exact SLA numbers in marketplace copy unless they’re standard and approved.

[14:10] Alex Chen: Agree.

[14:12] Ben Carter: Okay, we’re at 14 minutes; I want to make sure we leave with clear owners.

[14:17] Tyler Benson: Before that, quick question. Are there any restrictions on referencing “on-prem” or “air-gapped” in the marketplace listing? We offer it, but not via marketplace.

[14:26] Jordan Ellis: You can mention it as available, but not as the marketplace deliverable. Otherwise buyers expect a deployable artifact.

[14:34] Ben Carter: Cool.

[14:36] Camila Reyes: So action items: Ben will send a launch brief by Friday. Priya sends listing requirements. Soojin sends messaging blocks and claim rules. Tyler does UTM + lead routing plan.

[14:51] Alex Chen: Great. And I’ll reserve the week of July 28 editorial slot tentatively.

[14:57] Ben Carter: Perfect.

[15:00] (transcription note: conversation continues; minor overlaps)

[15:02] Alex Chen: Just to confirm, when do you think you can tell us “Arcadia vs QuantaPay”?

[15:08] Camila Reyes: By next Tuesday, June 24. We’ll have more clarity from the customer stakeholders.

[15:14] Priya Nair: Great.

[15:16] Jordan Ellis: And send any security positioning you want in the listing—encryption, audit logs, data retention. We can help format it.

[15:26] Soojin Lee: We’ll include the safe language: “no training on customer data” for Hosted, and retention configurable. But we’ll align with our official policy statements.

[15:37] Alex Chen: Perfect.

[15:39] Ben Carter: Alright, anything else from Nimbus side?

[15:42] Priya Nair: Not from me.

[15:44] Jordan Ellis: Nope.

[15:46] Alex Chen: All good. Thanks, everyone.

[15:49] Ben Carter: Thanks all. We’ll follow up in email with the recap and dates.

(End of transcript excerpt — Fireflies captured additional low-signal chatter after the recap.)
